# T009 — Patch frontend Vite and Rollup build family

## Summary

Patched the Vite 6/Rollup 4 production build and compatible CSS, React-plugin, and test-runner leaves. Clean Node 24 installation includes the matching Linux Rollup native binary; production build, TypeScript check, all 35 discovered tests, and lint pass. The dependency scan still reports findings outside this compatible build patch.

## Changes (files and why)

- `frontend/package.json`: Vite 6.4.4 (from locked 6.4.1) and Vitest 3.2.7 (from 3.2.4), without changing runtime application code or the test harness.
- `package.json`: match the explicit Linux optional Rollup binary to Rollup 4.64.12 (previously 4.52.5).
- `package-lock.json`: npm-managed resolution of the Vite/Rollup family and compatible transitive `postcss`, `nanoid`, `@babel/core`, `browserslist`, and `baseline-browser-mapping` patches. No direct production dependencies were added.

## Decisions (rationale and sources)

- Kept Vite on major 6, satisfying Spark's `^6.2.0` peer and Vitest 3's Vite peer range (`npm explain rollup`; `npm view vite@6.4.4 engines dependencies.rollup`; `npm view vitest@3.2.7 dependencies`). Vite advisory [GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm) describes a Windows-specific dev-server path; no app/ACS behavior changed. Rollup [GHSA-mw96-cpmx-2vgc](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mw96-cpmx-2vgc) concerns malicious build inputs; pinned native binary must match the resolved engine version. `npm update rollup` selected 4.64.12; `npm install --save-optional` aligned the root binary. Verified installed binary and locked entry after `npm ci`.
- The test-only [GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9) remains on Vitest 3.2.7; its unauthenticated exposure requires a reachable mocker dev server, not the current CLI-only `vitest run`. Current scanner proposes a Vitest **major** for the residual mocker/tinypool findings. Do not force that migration or claim the scan is clean; hand it to later audit closeout for a planned migration/owner decision.
- Advisory evidence: npm audit JSON generated by skill scanner on 2026-10-21, with advisory URLs in the JSON; selected GitHub advisories above independently consulted. Scanner: `/shared/skills/dependency-vulnerability-remediation/scripts/scan-dependencies.sh`; npm 11.19.0, Node 24.21.0. All patched packages are frontend direct development dependencies or their transitive build/test dependencies, so ordinary production requests do not call the vulnerable tool paths. Test-only dev-server exposure should still be assessed if externally exposed.

## Validation (commands and results)

All commands run from the repository root with `CI=true TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8`, on Node 24:

- `npm ci` — pass; installed Rollup 4.64.12 and `@rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu` 4.64.12, both in lock.
- `npm run build --if-present` — pass; Vite emitted three CSS optimization warnings (not suppressed).
- `npm test` — pass: backend 15, frontend 20, total **35 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `npm run lint --if-present` — pass with five existing warnings (zero errors).
- `npm exec --workspace frontend -- tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — pass.
- `bash /shared/skills/dependency-vulnerability-remediation/scripts/scan-dependencies.sh --output-dir .modernization-scratch/scan .` — exit **2**, findings remain: root 3 critical / 22 high / 6 moderate / 2 low affected package names (previously 3 / 28 / 7 / 3); backend unchanged 0 / 3 / 0 / 0. Counts are affected packages, not unique advisories, and backend overlaps root. Raw JSON is in ignored `.modernization-scratch/scan/`.

## Follow-ups and risks

- Vitest 3's mocker and tinypool advisories need a separately planned compatible major migration or documented owner decision; not accepted or suppressed here. Remaining root/backend findings belong to later task families, including frontend ESLint and static-web-apps CLI.
- Build reports three CSS optimization warnings; no output or tests were weakened to silence them. Deprecation warnings from clean install (`inflight`, `glob@7`, `rimraf@2`, `sudo-prompt`) remain in other tool chains.
